newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Zurich airport to set emissions-linked landing fee.
newsitem.headline: Zurich airport to set emissions-linked landing fee.

text.p: Zurich Airport will introduce an emmissions-linked landing fee on September 1 and is considering cutting transit passenger fees in a move that could save Swissair millions of dollars a year, officials said.

"The world's first emissions-linked landing fee will be introduced as of September 1, 1997 for all air transport companies serving Zurich Airport," Zurich's government said in response in a question in the cantonal legislature.
It did not give the precise amount, but said it would be a surcharge to the existing fee based on weight and be set according to emissions, just as is the existing noise surcharge.

The government said it was discussing reducing transit passenger fees as one way to help Swissair attain its goal of cutting airport costs by 20 million to 30 million Swiss francs to levels other airlines in Europe face.
"Reducing transit passenger fees, which should be lower than the 15.50 Swiss franc tariff now in effect for all departing passengers, is at the forefront of negotiations with Swissair," it said.
Local passengers can simply be charged the fee, but airlines pay for transit passengers and cover the cost in ticket prices.
It noted Geneva airport introduced a system last month in which transit passengers pay 10 francs and local passengers 16 instead of the uniform 15.50 charge.
"Having the same rules for transit passengers in Zurich would save Swissair around 15 million francs a year," it said.
The lost revenue would not affect plans to expand the airport, it added.
